summary:
NOT VERIFIED OR NOT RIGHT, first:
1. Nothing was judged in motion. Shimmer, shading pops and cracks while tiles settle are unseen; I have stills and numbers only (mesh height under fixed spots moves at most 7 mm per frame around the landing place during a descent, up to 0.36 m in one frame off to the side, which is 0.27 px there).
2. The check on the real ports used my own script, not scripts/dev.ts: Alpha on 8420 and Beta on 8421 with the identities of universe 16, the client from packages/client/dist after `npm run build`, but data in memory (I was told not to touch .data), and the ship was put over the base by writing server state, not flown. scripts/e2e.mjs has NOT been run with terrain switched on; I switched it on for the game (ALL_PARTS), so the browser-test engineer's next build carries it.
3. Frame times are from the dev page on one moon, in headless Chromium with GPU, while other engineers used the machine, and were taken before my last shader fix (parent normal turn). Nothing was timed in the built game.
4. Never exercised: far view above the hand-over height in the built game, a lost WebGL context, a quality switch while playing, leaving a body and coming back, GPU memory, any browser but Chromium.
5. The 24 required screenshots were read as four half-size contact sheets plus named full-size crops, not one by one at full size. The full-size shots I opened one by one (c1/) predate my fixes.
6. One condition on the shared terrain is not met on large bodies and was not before me either: a full-detail sample costs 3.08 us on an 8,000 km rocky planet (old file 3.08, new file 3.08; under 2.8 us on the other four bodies measured).
7. Defects left in, all seen: a pale disc of 800 m radius around every base at noon (the pad's fixed tone 0.5); at low sun the small relief ends in a visible band about 70 to 110 m from a camera 8 m up; ice ridges still read as a dense scribble from 50 km and as a pixel-scale pattern from 300 km (their shape is height, which I did not change); fan-shaped rays around fresh craters look painted from 500 m; near ground is soft at high sun; the base model's ground plate shows as a smooth disc with an edge against the regolith.

This was a resumed task. Two earlier sessions of this role (they called themselves A and B) built nearly all of it between 06:20 and 07:10 and ended without a report: the whole of packages/client/src/render/local/terrain/, the far view in space/Bodies.ts and planetShader.ts, the dev page options and dev/hud.ts. I read all of it, found it working on the dev page, and did the rest.

What is now true: the game draws the ground of landable bodies (terrain is in ALL_PARTS). The built client loads four terrain workers and draws tiles with no console error or warning, on my own port and on 8420. On the test moon of universe 16 the drawn mesh is the shared terrain to a median of 0.4 mm within 30 m of a landed camera (max 7 cm at a small crater), and a landed ship's belly is within 1.4 mm of the drawn surface. A landed scene does not jitter (ground pixels differ by at most 1 of 255 over two seconds). Descents ran at 60.6 frames per second with no frame over 21.4 ms. I fixed three defects of the inherited code (skirts showing through far ground, straight seams between large tiles, 89 MB of dead texture copies) and retuned the tone of the shared terrain in three places with heights bit-identical. Final tree: tsc clean for all three packages, 40 test files, 606 passed, 2 expected fail (baseline 605; one test is new).
behaviour:
TILES (render/local/terrain/tiles.ts, inherited; my changes marked). Cube sphere with six faces, a quadtree per face, 32 mesh cells along a tile edge. A tile is split while the camera is nearer than 2 of its edge lengths (stays split to 2.2), ground outside the view is kept 2.5 times coarser by distance. Deepest level: cells of 1.25 to 2.5 m (level 15 with 1.58 m cells on the 1,057 km test moon, level 16 on the 2,310 km desert planet). Map texels per cell: 4 at quality 2, 2 below, never under 0.6 m. A parent is always baked before its children and is replaced only when all four are there. At most 4 baked tiles go to the GPU per frame, coarse first; groups of four unused for 4 s are dropped; the tiles of a body are freed 15 s after the camera leaves it. Vertices slide onto the parent's surface over the last 9 % of the distance at which the parent takes over; a new tile settles from the parent's surface in 0.5 s. Tiles beyond 2 km are drawn far to near, each back to front, because the depth buffer of the local scene (0.5 m to 400 km) steps by tens of metres there; ground beyond the far plane is kept at the far plane's depth. MINE: tiles beyond SKIRT_RANGE = 20 km are drawn without their skirt (skirt depth is 1.5 cells). MINE: a tile reads its parent's normal map through a rotation from the parent's frame into its own (uFromParent). MINE: the CPU copy of a tile's map is released once uploaded.

HAND-OVER (relief.ts, inherited). handoverAltitude = max(radius, 100 km): 1,057 km on the test moon. Above it the body is the space layer's far view alone. Below it tiles are drawn, flat at that height, with relief growing 0 to 1 (smoothstep) down to half that height. While tiles are drawn the far view's sphere sinks to terrainMin - 200 m.

FAR VIEW (farmap.ts, space/Bodies.ts, planetShader.ts, inherited). A landable body larger than 12 px in radius gets a cube map of 512 x 512 texels per face (3.2 km per texel on the test moon), half floats: slope vector and tone, baked by the same workers in 8 strips per face. Until it is ready the procedural look stays; the map fades in over 1.5 s. At most 4 maps are kept, an unused one at least 20 s. Bodies.ts takes the rotation from the shared bodyRotation. Without the terrain part (space dev page) landable bodies keep the procedural look.

WORKERS (pool.ts, worker.ts, inherited). min(4, cores / 2) workers; jobs wait on the main thread by priority (tiles in view, then far-map strips, then tiles outside the view) and can be cancelled until they start. The built worker is one self-contained file of 10.7 kB with the terrain function, the bake and the cube sphere.

LIGHT (material.ts, shade.ts, inherited). Sun and ambient are the frame's Lighting, the same numbers the objects part gives its lights. Reflectance is 70 % Lambert and 30 % Lommel-Seeliger; the terminator is a smoothstep of the sun's height over -0.012..0.008. The shadow is three's shadow map of the objects part's sun; ground behind the shadow box is tested at the box's end and the shadow fades over 70 box widths. Spot and point lights add diffuse light; the camera's fill light is left out. Small relief below the terrain's 10 m: five octaves of gradient noise with cells of 5.3 m, 1.6 m, 0.5 m, 0.16 m and 5 cm, shading only, each shown while a pixel covers less than 0.14 to 0.42 of its cell; none at quality 0. Albedo follows the body's base colour per class (rocky 0.30 + 1.50 tone, ice a mix of dust and bright ice, desert 0.42 + 1.15 tone).

SHARED TERRAIN, TONE ONLY (packages/shared/src/universe/terrain.ts). Heights are bit-identical: 0 of 48 generator rows and 0 of 100,000 random directions on five bodies differ; 22 of 48 generator tones differ (rocky 9, ice 10, desert 3), 13 of the 28 golden rows of terrain.test.ts were rewritten.
(1) Ejecta of fresh craters. Before: bright = t^2 * rays, with rays = 0.3 + 0.7 * ray^2, which stepped at the rim from 1.0 inside to 0.3..1.0 outside. After: bright = t^2 * (rays + (1 - rays) * t^4): 1.0 at the rim, the rays alone farther out.
(2) Ice. Before: tone = 0.74 + 0.14 high + 0.06 mottle - 0.4 crest + 0.3 craterTone, crest = max of the two ridge profiles to the eighth power; a coarse sample that skips the ridges got crest 0. After: tone = 0.72 + 0.16 high + 0.09 mottle - ICE_BAND_DARK * band * (1 - 0.85 high) + 0.3 craterTone, ICE_BAND_DARK = 0.2, band = smooth(0.37, 0.78, max of the two profiles to the fourth power); a coarse sample gets band = ICE_BAND_MEAN = 0.56. Mean tone of full against coarse samples now differs by 0.001 (before about 0.15 * the band share).
(3) Desert. Before: the dune mask and the dunes were evaluated only when detail <= 320 m; coarser samples had no dune tone and were 0.032 darker on average. After: the mask is evaluated whenever its wavelength allows, and a sample too coarse for single dunes gets dune = mask * DUNE_MEAN, DUNE_MEAN = 0.63, for the tone only; mean difference now under 0.001.
Cost of a full-detail sample, best of 7 over 300,000 directions, old file (4a9e7f1) / tree, Node 22.14 on a loaded machine: rocky 1,737 km 2.77 / 2.76 us; ice 800 km 1.61 / 1.60; desert 3,400 km 2.52 / 2.53; rocky 8,000 km 3.08 / 3.08; rocky 1,057 km 2.62 / 2.61. Slope share is unchanged because heights are: rocky 1,000 km 91.1 % under 15 degrees over 20 m, rocky 350 km 93.0 %, rocky 8,000 km 91.7 %, ice 98.8 %, desert 99.4 %.

MEMORY. About 1,005 tiles are loaded near the ground at quality 2 (up to 1,082 seen). Array buffers after a forced collection: 187 MB before my change, 98 MB after; JS heap 20 MB. GPU memory not measured (by size of the maps roughly the 89 MB that left the CPU, plus mip levels). Each far map keeps 12.6 MB on the CPU as well, at most four.
names: render/local/index.ts ALL_PARTS = ['objects', 'fx', 'terrain'] - the game now loads the terrain part (changed by me); PartName in part.ts has 'terrain'
render/local/terrain/index.ts createTerrain(): Part - the part; reads view.surface (body, rot, cam) and bodyTerrain(view.system, body)
render/local/terrain/index.ts terrainDebug { ground, stats, relief, shown, updateMs } - what the part is doing, for the dev page and measurements; not used by the game

render/local/terrain/tiles.ts class Ground - the quadtree of one body; update(cam, right, up, forward, tanY, aspect, clock, show); heightAt(dir, relief): height of the drawn mesh under a direction this frame, or null; levelAt(dir); covered; stats: GroundStats { loaded, drawn, waiting, level, deepest, uploads, selectMs, uploadMs, total }

render/local/terrain/tiles.ts CELLS = 32 (exported); constants SPLIT 2, KEEP 1.1, MORPH_START 0.91, OUTSIDE 2.5, FADE_IN 0.5 s, FAR_ORDER 2,000 m, UPLOADS 4, IDLE 4 s, MIN_TEXEL 0.6 m; new: SKIRT_RANGE = 20,000 m, SKIRT_INDICES

render/local/terrain/cube.ts FACES, faceTangent, faceDirection, facePoint, directionToFace, tileSpan, tileSize, tileFrame, deepestLevel; new: frameTurn(from, to, out) - rotation from one tile frame into another, nine numbers row by row

render/local/terrain/bake.ts bakeTile(params, TileSpec): TileBake, bakeFarRows(params, face, size, row0, rows), gridDetail, skirtDepth, skirtAnchor, tileVertexCount, tileIndexCount, tileIndices, tileOrder, tileUvs, toHalf, fromHalf - everything the worker computes; pure
render/local/terrain/pool.ts terrainPool(): TerrainPool with body(key, params), forget(key), tile(...), far(...), available, pending - the shared worker pool; worker.ts WorkerRequest, WorkerResult

render/local/terrain/material.ts tileMaterial(shared), groundUniforms(): GroundUniforms { uRadius, uRelief, uFar, uBase, uKind, uDetail, uSunView, uSunColor, uAmbient }, mapTexture, DETAIL_PERIOD = 4096 m; new per-tile uniform uFromParent (mat3)
render/local/terrain/shade.ts GROUND_GLSL (cubeWarp, groundAlbedo, groundLit) and groundKind(cls) - colour and lighting shared by tiles and far view
render/local/terrain/farmap.ts enableFarMaps(), farMap(sys, bodyId, clock): FarMap { texture, readyAt } | null, disposeFarMaps()
render/local/terrain/relief.ts handoverAltitude(radius), reliefAt(radius, dist), FAR_SPHERE_MARGIN = 200 m, groundShown { system, body, relief } - written by the terrain part, read by Bodies.ts
shared universe/terrain.ts new constants ICE_BAND_DARK = 0.2, ICE_BAND_MEAN = 0.56, DUNE_MEAN = 0.63 (tone only; interface unchanged)
